The Portrait of Henry VIII by Hans Holbein the Younger is one of the most iconic images of the English monarch. In this portrait, Henry VIII is depicted standing with a confident and imposing posture. He is wearing elaborate clothing and a large chain of office. Importantly, in his right hand, he is holding a single glove, which was a common symbol of nobility and authority during that period.

There is no historical or artistic record of Henry VIII holding a turkey leg in this portrait. The idea of a turkey leg is more associated with modern or informal depictions, not this formal royal portrait.

Therefore, the correct answer is that King Henry is holding a glove.

Answer: A
